signature.name: Red Fort
signature.detail: The Mughal emperor's red sandstone fortress and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the setting for India's Independence Day address. Go early in the morning to beat the heat and crowds, and note that foreign visitors pay a higher ticket than locals.

signature.name: Qutub Minar
signature.detail: A soaring 73-metre victory tower from the 12th century, the tallest brick minaret in the world, surrounded by early Indo-Islamic tombs. Visit in the late afternoon for softer light; it is a short ride south of central Delhi.

signature.name: India Gate
signature.detail: The grand war memorial arch at the end of Rajpath, best seen lit up after dark when locals gather on the lawns. Come in the evening; there is no entry fee for the surrounding area.

signature.name: Humayun's Tomb
signature.detail: The garden tomb that inspired the Taj Mahal, a serene UNESCO-listed Mughal monument. Go at opening time for quiet paths and good photos; tickets are sold at the gate.

signature.name: Lotus Temple
signature.detail: A striking flower-shaped Bahai house of worship open to all faiths, known for its calm silent hall. Entry is free but you must remove your shoes and keep quiet inside; it is closed on Mondays.

transport: Metro $0.25-0.60 a ride; auto-rickshaws and taxis cheap
